correctness.rationale: Nontrivial ψ makes (s,y)↦ψ(sy) a nondegenerate character pairing, even over extension fields: for nonzero y multiplication by y is a bijection. Invert in s; equality of quadratic labels factors as (t−u)(t+u−c)=0. The fiber equations give antisymmetry under t↦c−t, including zero at c/2. Composing with the c₀ reflection produces all translations generated by c−c₀; over characteristic p that additive subgroup is exactly H_C, independently of c₀. The converse follows by factoring each reflection using the c₀ reflection and a translation. On F/H_C the shifted reflection has one fixed point and (q/h−1)/2 opposite pairs, proving the claimed nullity and rank. Each active pair contributes exactly 2h support coordinates, with equality on a single pair; the two indicators then attain failure at sparsity h. The full-span case is injective without a sparsity restriction. Full span requires affine dimension m, with equality in view count exactly for an affine basis, and the distinct lines intersect only at the origin.
residual_risks: Only complete nonhorizontal Fourier lines and odd characteristic are included. The example ranks are finite corroboration, not proof of the general law or evidence for conditioning under noise.

value.rationale: A view count by itself can be misleading in extension fields: over F₉ three offsets {0,1,2} leave only a one-dimensional span and admit a collision on two 3-site cosets, whereas {0,1,ω} for ω outside F₃ is injective. The exact span invariant explains the difference and supplies an immediately usable test for rank, worst-case sparse identifiability, and how many complete views to acquire. The prescribed-line restriction is integral to the problem, not a claim about optimal arbitrary samples.
residual_risks: Value is about exact measurements and identifiability, not a stability guarantee, a reconstruction complexity bound, or arbitrary single-frequency sample optimization.
